title: Regulated Vertical Playbook — Fintech, Healthcare, Legal, Enterprise SaaS, Gov/Defense (Draft)
content:
Context:
This is a working playbook for GTM messaging and early field experiments across regulated / compliance-heavy verticals: fintech, healthcare, legal, enterprise SaaS (security-sensitive), and government/defense. Purpose is to capture hypotheses, one-liners, primary buyer personas, competitive notes, pilot metrics, and immediate asks for product/engineering and legal. Not polished—intended for SDRs, AEs, and solutions engineering to iterate quickly.

Top-level hypothesis:
- Redwood's primary differentiation for regulated customers is not model quality alone but predictable, auditable inference with deployment flexibility: hosted with strong tenancy controls, Dedicated capacity with SLAs, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for full data control.
- Messaging should lead with reliability, data isolation, and measurable unit economics (cost/token) rather than feature laundry list.

Quick play summary (1-line for each vertical):
- Fintech: "Run LLM inference behind your firewall with predictable latency, auditable prompts, and cost controls—built for regulated money flows."
- Healthcare: "HIPAA-conscious inference that keeps PHI on-prem or in your VPC while giving care teams reliable, low-latency assistive models."
- Legal: "Traceable, versioned model rollouts and deterministic prompts for defensible legal research and contract automation."
- Enterprise SaaS: "Reduce inference spend and delivery variance across customers with Dedicated instances + per-customer routing and cost observability."
- Gov/Defense: "Air-gapped/private deployment options with KMS/HSM integrations and FIPS-aligned audit trails."

Primary buyer personas (per vertical):
- Fintech: Head of Engineering (payments/transactions), Head of ML/AI, Chief Risk Officer, Compliance Manager
- Healthcare: Chief Medical Information Officer (CMIO), Head of Engineering, Privacy Officer, Clinical Ops Director
- Legal: Head of Legal Ops, Director of Knowledge Management, Senior Counsel (IP/Contracts)
- Enterprise SaaS: VP Product, Platform Engineering Manager, Head of Customer Success (for integrations)
- Gov/Defense: CTO/Platform Lead, Security Architect, Program Manager (contracting)

Common pain points we can solve (cross-vertical):
- Uncertain inference costs and token spend variability
- Data leakage / PHI/PII exposure concerns with public cloud APIs
- Lack of predictable latency for user-facing workflows
- No clear audit trail or model/version provenance for regulatory reviews
- Difficulty running canary/rollouts safely across tenants

Proof points / quantifiable claims to validate with Product team (draft metrics):
- 95th percentile latency numbers on Dedicated pools for 2kQPS workloads (target: <120ms per token for small-medium models)
- Typical cost reduction via batching + KV caching: 30–60% on long-context generation use cases
- Number of customers in beta on Private deployments (privacy-sensitive): current = 4 (need to validate)
- Outage MTTR targets and SLAs: 99.9% uptime for Dedicated (proposal)

Competitive landscape notes (quick bullets, not exhaustive):
- General cloud AI providers (major clouds): strong on enterprise integration and billing; weak on turnkey private/on-prem inference experiences that are optimized for cost.
- LLM API startups: simple dev ergonomics but limited on dedicated capacity SLAs and private deployments.
- Open-source runtimes/self-hosted vendors: attractive on control but high ops burden and variable performance tradeoffs (engineering-heavy).
- How Redwood needs to position: "we're the production-grade middle ground"—developer ergonomics + operational SLAs + private deployment options.

Per-vertical tactical messaging, objections, and rebuttals:
- Fintech:
  * Hook: "No transaction data leaves your VPC unless you allow it — and you can measure the cost per approval/denial in cents."
  * Key questions: custody of logs, retention policies, ability to redact and replay prompts for audits.
  * Rebuttal to "we just use cloud vendor API": point to dedicated throughput predictability and explicit routing/fallbacks to cheaper model variants during spikes (cost control).
  * Pilot KPI: reduce fraud-review average handle time by 25% while maintaining false positive rate within +/- 2%.

- Healthcare:
  * Hook: "Deploy with PHI never leaving your network; integrated KMS and audit trails for every inference."
  * Objections: HIPAA BAAs, encryption-at-rest/in-transit, model hallucination risk.
  * Rebuttal: offer pilot with de-identified test dataset and logging controls; emphasize ability to pin model versions and perform regression evals on clinical prompts.
  * Pilot KPI: accelerate chart summarization time by 40% and measure clinician correction rate.

- Legal:
  * Hook: "Versioned models + prompt provenance = defensible outputs for legal research and contract drafting."
  * Objections: bias, fidelity, admissibility.
  * Rebuttal: show audit trail UI and ability to freeze model+prompt+context for a given delivered output; produce exportable evidence artifacts for reviews.
  * Pilot KPI: reduce contract review time for standard NDAs by 35% with <1% critical omission rate.

- Enterprise SaaS:
  * Hook: "Per-tenant Dedicated routing and cost observability so you stop losing margin on AI features."
  * Objections: complexity of managing per-tenant infra.
  * Rebuttal: Redwood handles routing and autoscaling—customer sees simple API and cost dashboard.
  * Pilot KPI: increase margin on premium AI tier by 10% through batching/quantization playbook.

- Gov/Defense:
  * Hook: "Private control plane and on-prem packages with KMS/HSM integrations and FIPS guidance."
  * Objections: supply chain, accreditation, FedRAMP/CMMC requirements.
  * Rebuttal: outline path to common controls mapping; initial pilots can be non-classified testbeds (air-gapped).
  * Pilot KPI: pass initial security review checklist for Low/Moderate IL systems (example).

Suggested GTM experiments (quick):
- Run 3 pilot offers (one per cluster) with an SOW template: fintech fraud-review, healthcare chart-summarization, enterprise SaaS per-tenant routing pilot. Measure cost per successful transaction and latency percentiles.
- Create vertical-specific one-pagers and short customer-ready demo flows (5–7 minute demo scripts).
- Structured A/B messaging test on website landing for "data-protected inference" vs "low-cost inference" with contact-capture forms.
- Sales enablement: battlecards for the 3 primary competitors per vertical.

Suggested collateral (MVP set):
- Fintech one-pager + demo repo (sample integration with card-processing flow)
- Healthcare whiteboard + compliance checklist (HIPAA BAAs, de-identification approach)
- Legal playbook + exportable audit artifact example (PDF evidence package)
- Enterprise SaaS ROI calculator (spreadsheet, quick numbers)
- Gov/Defense checklist with KMS/HSM and air-gapped deployment notes

Open questions / TODOs for cross-functional owners:
- Legal: confirm standard BAA language and turnaround time for Private customers. (Owner: Legal, ticket GT-3421)
- Product: finalize Dedicated SLA wording and latency targets. Can we commit to numeric 95th/99th percentiles? (Owner: Eng-Serving-Runtime)
- Security: produce a short FIPS/CIS mapping doc for initial Gov/Defense conversations. (Owner: Security & Compliance)
- Solutions Eng: create 3 demo scripts and a trimmed dataset for pilot customers. (Owner: Solutions Eng)

Launch checklist (pre-pilot):
- Sales kit: one-pager, battlecard, pricing SLA (draft) -> deadline: 2025-02-10
- Legal: BAA + Private deployment SOW templates -> deadline: 2025-02-17
- Product/Eng: Dedicated SLA and performance report for pilot clusters -> deadline: 2025-02-14
- Demo infra: 3 reproducible demo projects in GitHub -> deadline: 2025-02-21

Notes / rough copy for outreach emails (iterate):
- Subject: "Secure, auditable LLM inference for [Company] — pilot offer"
- Body lead: "Hi <name>, we help teams in <vertical> run LLMs with predictable latency, auditable prompts, and private deployment options. Would you be open to a 6-week pilot to measure accuracy, latency, and cost vs. your current approach?"

Psychographic hooks to test in messaging (A/B ideas):
- "Defensible outputs" vs "Low-cost predictable inference" vs "PHI-first privacy controls"
- Lead with outcome (reduced review time) vs. lead with control (private deploy + audit)

Concluding notes (meta):
- This doc intentionally mixes tactical and strategic thinking; please pull out the bits you need for your flow.
- Next sync: quick review with solutions eng + legal on 2025-02-05 to iron out BAAs and pilot SOW language.
- If you take this into a Confluence page, leave a link back here and mark as 'in_review' once we have product sign-off.

Raw ideas / scraps (scratchpad):
- Partner idea: compliance consult firms (HIPAA, SOC2 auditors) co-sell for healthcare/gov pilots.
- Pricing experiment: time-boxed reserved capacity credits for first 3 pilots (reduce friction).
- Slack followups: #gtm-verticals thread contains early customer intros.

END.
